threadiverse.fetchPluggable: YES — fully injectable and the cleanest part of the package. Constructor is `new ThreadiverseClient(hostname: string, options: BaseClientOptions)` where `interface BaseClientOptions { fetchFunction?: typeof fetch; headers?: Record<string,string> }` (index.d.ts:13062-13065). Runtime wiring: PieFed client `this.#customFetch = options.fetchFunction ?? globalThis.fetch` (index.mjs:3494) and `const fetch = options?.fetchFunction ?? globalThis.fetch` (index.mjs:4165). Lemmy v0/v1 clients pass the entire options object straight into lemmy-js-client's LemmyHttp (`new LemmyV1.LemmyHttp(hostname, options)`, index.mjs:2574), and LemmyHttp does `_fetchFunction = fetch.bind(globalThis)` by default, overridden by `options.fetchFunction` (lemmy-js-client-v0/dist/http.js:46,52-53). So Janus supplies RN's global fetch via `fetchFunction: fetch.bind(globalThis)` OR omits it (defaults to globalThis.fetch, which RN provides). This is exactly how Voyager wires it in services/client.ts (`fetchFunction: usingNativeFetch ? nativeFetch : fetch.bind(globalThis)`) — Janus simply drops the Capacitor `nativeFetch` shim (services/nativeFetch.ts, which reassigns window.fetch/XMLHttpRequest) and passes RN fetch. Auth is via `headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <jwt>', ... }` — no token store coupling.
threadiverse.uploadImageSignature: TS signature (index.d.ts:13283-13285, on abstract BaseClient and surfaced on ThreadiverseClient): `uploadImage(payload: { image: File }, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<UploadImageResponse>` where UploadImageResponse = { url: string; delete_token?: string } (z.infer of UploadImageResponse$1) and RequestOptions = Pick<RequestInit,"signal">. THE highest-risk call. The declared param type is the browser DOM `File`, which does not exist under Hermes/JSC. BUT the RUNTIME is more permissive: PieFed path builds `new FormData(); formData.append('file', payload.image)` then POSTs via the injectable fetch (index.mjs:4116-4127) — FormData.append accepts anything. Lemmy path delegates to lemmy-js-client createFormData, which does `if (image instanceof File) append(image) else append(new Blob([image],{type:'image/jpeg'}),'image.jpg')` (lemmy-js-client-v0 http.js:1027-1037, v1 http.js identical block ~2139). So in RN you can pass an RN FormData file descriptor `{ uri, name, type }` (cast to File to satisfy TS) on the PieFed/raw-FormData path; for the Lemmy `instanceof File` branch you'd fall into the Blob branch (RN Blob from a fetch().blob() or a base64-backed Blob) OR provide a File polyfill. Voyager passes a real browser File (services/lemmy.ts:27-51) after compressing via canvas (helpers/imageCompress.ts) — both are browser-only and are Voyager APP code, not threadiverse; Janus replaces compression with expo-image-manipulator and feeds an RN file object.
threadiverse.pageCursorShape: `type PageCursor = number | string` (index.d.ts:12844, exported as PageCursor). Request pagination: `type PageParams = { limit?: number; page_cursor?: PageCursor }` (index.d.ts:12840-12843); most list methods take `PageParams & {...}` (e.g. listPersonSaved, listPostReports, GetNotifications = PageParams & {type_?, unread_only?}). Response pagination: paginated responses spread a `PagableResponse` shape = `{ next_page?: string | number; prev_page?: string | number }` (zod PagableResponse$1, index.d.ts:2007-2010 / type at 13039) — built at runtime by toPageResponse/toPageResponse$1. Next page is expressed by passing the response's `next_page` value back in as `page_cursor`. This unifies Lemmy's opaque string page_cursor (v0/v1) and PieFed's numeric page into one number|string cursor — a clean opaque-cursor model that maps directly to TanStack Query / FlashList infinite-scroll getNextPageParam.
threadiverse.notificationModel: Fully unified/consolidated across Lemmy v0/v1/PieFed into one abstraction. A single `Notification` type (zod Notification$1, index.d.ts:1569-1586) with a discriminator `kind: 'subscribed' | 'private_message' | 'mod_action' | 'reply' | 'mention'` (NotificationDataType enum, index.d.ts:1561-1567) plus fields id, creator_id, recipient_id, read, published_at, and optional comment_id/post_id/private_message_id/modlog_id. `NotificationView` (index.d.ts:1587+) is a discriminated union carrying the underlying comment/post/PM/modlog data. Unified methods on BaseClient/ThreadiverseClient: `getNotifications(payload: GetNotifications, opts?)` where GetNotifications = PageParams & { type_?: 'all' | NotificationDataType; unread_only?: boolean } returns ListNotificationsResponse (paginated); `getUnreadCount() -> GetUnreadCountResponse`; `markNotificationAsRead({ kind: NotificationDataType; notification_id: number; read: boolean })` (index.d.ts:13232-13236); `markAllAsRead()`. This is the package's biggest value-add for Janus: it collapses Lemmy's separate replies/mentions/private-messages endpoints and PieFed's notification model into one inbox stream with a single kind discriminator and one unread count — exactly the consolidation a custom client would otherwise have to hand-roll.
hermesRisks: uploadImage param typed as DOM `File` (index.d.ts:13284) — File is undefined under Hermes/JSC. Not a crash on import (it's only a type + a runtime `instanceof File` guard that simply evaluates false in RN), but you must feed an RN-shaped FormData file object or a Blob and TS-cast. Highest-risk single call.

RN FormData semantics differ from web: RN FormData.append wants `{ uri, name, type }` descriptors, not File/Blob; the lemmy-js-client `new Blob([image],...)` fallback branch (http.js:1034) needs RN to have a working Blob that fetch can serialize as multipart — RN's Blob support for multipart bodies is workable but historically finicky; test the actual pictrs upload on-device early.

@tsoa/runtime (transitive via lemmy-js-client-v1, statically imported in index.mjs) pulls `reflect-metadata` at load (index.js:17). reflect-metadata is the polyfill itself and runs under Hermes, but it expects to install Reflect.* — generally fine, just adds bundle weight and a global side effect.

@tsoa/runtime re-exports express/koa/hapi route-template barrels (index.js:34). Those frameworks are referenced as TYPES only (no require('express') at load), so they should be tree-shaken/never-executed — but Metro will still walk/resolve express & @hapi during bundling, which can surface resolution warnings or pull a chunk of dead server code into the bundle. Verify with a Metro build; may need resolver exclusions or a metro.config blockList.
Pure-ESM only (.mjs). Metro handles ESM, but Jest/test setups and any CJS-assuming tooling need transformIgnorePatterns/babel config to process node_modules/threadiverse and the lemmy-js-client deps.

No top-level await observed in dist (import-time is synchronous class definitions) — low risk. No atob/btoa/document/window/localStorage/XMLHttpRequest anywhere in threadiverse or lemmy-js-client dist, so no base64/DOM polyfill is needed for the client itself.
threadiverse.verdict: YES — the LemmyAdapter can depend on threadiverse@0.14.2 in React Native, with a small, well-scoped set of shims. The core surface is RN-friendly: pure-fetch transport with a first-class injectable `fetchFunction` (BaseClientOptions, index.d.ts:13062) defaulting to globalThis.fetch, JWT auth purely via a `headers` map, no DOM/Node API usage anywhere in threadiverse's own dist (grep found zero hits for window/document/atob/btoa/localStorage/XMLHttpRequest/node:/fs/process), opaque number|string PageCursor that drops straight into infinite-scroll, and a genuinely unified notification inbox across Lemmy v0/v1/PieFed. The Capacitor `nativeFetch` shim Voyager uses (services/nativeFetch.ts) is dropped entirely — Janus just passes RN's global fetch. REQUIRED SHIMS / WORK, in priority order: (1) uploadImage is the only real friction — the TS type demands a browser `File` but the runtime accepts FormData-appendable values; supply an RN FormData file descriptor `{ uri, name, type }` (TS-cast to File) or an RN Blob, and replace Voyager's canvas-based compressor (helpers/imageCompress.ts) with expo-image-manipulator; on-device test the multipart pictrs upload first. (2) Bundle/Metro hygiene for the @tsoa/runtime chain dragged in by lemmy-js-client-v1 (statically imported): include `reflect-metadata` (it self-installs under Hermes), and add a Metro resolver blockList/exclusion so express/@hapi/koa template barrels (referenced only as types, never required at load) don't bloat or noise the bundle. (3) Ensure Metro + Jest transform node_modules/threadiverse and the two lemmy-js-client packages as ESM (transformIgnorePatterns). NOT needed: base64/URL/DOM polyfills for the client itself. If the @tsoa/runtime/express resolution proves intractable in Metro (unlikely but possible), the fallback is to depend on `lemmy-js-client` directly (the v0 package has ZERO deps) and hand-roll the PieFed path — but that sacrifices exactly threadiverse's value: the v0/v1/PieFed software auto-detection via .well-known, the unified sort/listing conversion layer, the consolidated notification inbox + single unread count, and the Zod runtime response validation. Recommendation: adopt threadiverse, isolate it behind LemmyAdapter, and de-risk the uploadImage path with an on-device spike before committing.

reddit.transportSummary: CONFIRMED single global native cookie jar, implicit attachment. The transport never sets a Cookie header. Flow: (1) The api() chokepoint in api/RedditApi.ts sets only X-Modhash (line 29, from the UserAuth.modhash singleton in api/Authentication.ts), User-Agent (line 39), and Content-Type for POST bodies (line 35). It then calls safeFetch (line 41). (2) safeFetch (utils/safeFetch.ts) is an XMLHttpRequest wrapper; it loops fetchOptions.headers and calls xhr.setRequestHeader for each (lines 55-57), plus cache headers (line 69). It NEVER sets Cookie and never sets withCredentials. The reddit_session cookie is therefore attached IMPLICITLY by the native iOS layer (RCTHTTPRequestHandler -> NSURLSession -> shared NSHTTPCookieStorage), not by JS. (3) RedditCookies (utils/RedditCookies.ts) is the only writer/reader of that jar, all host-keyed to https://www.reddit.com via @preeternal/react-native-cookie-manager (CookieManager.set/get/clearAll on lines 10, 22, 27, 41, 49, 65-72). So auth = global host-keyed jar (cookie) + a single process-global modhash. A grep across api/ utils/ contexts/ found zero explicit Cookie headers anywhere in the app.
reddit.cookieHeaderControl: No, not reliably on iOS. safeFetch CAN syntactically call xhr.setRequestHeader("Cookie", ...) since it blindly forwards any header (utils/safeFetch.ts lines 55-57), but on iOS that header does not give reliable per-request control. RN routes XHR through RCTHTTPRequestHandler -> NSURLSession with the shared NSHTTPCookieStorage and default httpShouldHandleCookies=YES; JS cannot set httpShouldHandleCookies=NO per request, so the native shared jar still participates and a manually-injected Cookie header is unreliable (notably dropped/not carried across the 30x redirects Reddit login uses). The app deliberately never does this; it manages the single shared jar via CookieManager instead. So effective per-request Cookie control from JS = NO on iOS.
reddit.iosLimitation: On iOS, cookie handling is owned by the native networking layer, not RN JS. NSURLSession defaults to httpShouldHandleCookies=YES, which auto-injects matching cookies from the shared NSHTTPCookieStorage; a manually-set Cookie header on an NSMutableURLRequest overrides the store ONLY at the native level, and RN's XHR/RCTHTTPRequestHandler does not expose httpShouldHandleCookies per request to JS. Worse, RN on iOS has a long-standing, still-open bug where cookies and auth headers are DROPPED across redirects (facebook/react-native#15918, re-opened as #26311), which matters because Reddit's web login/session flow is redirect-heavy; the accepted fix is patching RCTHTTPRequestHandler.mm to add NSURLSessionTaskDelegate and re-inject NSHTTPCookieStorage cookies in willPerformHTTPRedirection. Net: per-request Cookie headers from JS are not a supported, reliable mechanism on iOS. Citations: https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/15918 ; https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/26311 ; Apple httpShouldHandleCookies https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsurlrequest/httpshouldhandlecookies ; React Native Networking docs https://reactnative.dev/docs/network
reddit.rewriteScope: To get TRUE concurrent Reddit accounts you would have to break out of the shared native jar, which means a native-level transport, not a JS tweak. Scope: (1) safeFetch/api transport: replace the XHR path for Reddit with a custom native module (or patched RCTHTTPRequestHandler.mm) that sets httpShouldHandleCookies=NO and explicitly injects a per-account Cookie: reddit_session=... header, AND re-injects it in willPerformHTTPRedirection to survive Reddit's redirects (RN bug #15918/#26311). This is a native iOS (and matching Android) change plus an Expo prebuild/config-plugin or ejected native code -- non-trivial, and it fights the platform. (2) RedditCookies.ts: today every method is hardcoded to the single host key https://www.reddit.com (lines 10, 22, 41, 49, 65-72); persist/clear logic and the clearAll(true) WebKit-sync bug workaround (lines 53-72, referencing react-native-cookies PR #152) all assume one jar. For concurrency you would stop writing reddit_session into the live jar entirely and instead hold each account's session string in memory/SecureStore and pass it per request -- making most of RedditCookies obsolete or rewritten. (3) Authentication.ts: the modhash MUST stop being a process-global singleton (UserAuth.modhash) and become per-account, threaded into every api() call and every X-Modhash header (api/RedditApi.ts line 29). (4) WebView login (components/Modals/Login.tsx) FUNDAMENTALLY depends on the shared jar: sharedCookiesEnabled={true} + thirdPartyCookiesEnabled={true} (lines 154-155) and hasSessionCookieBeenSet() polling (lines 122-128) work precisely because WKWebView writes reddit_session into the same shared NSHTTPCookieStorage the app reads. If you remove the app's reliance on that shared jar, login still lands the cookie in the shared store, so you must capture it post-login and immediately evict it from the live jar (or move login into an ephemeral/isolated WKWebsiteDataStore) to avoid it leaking as the implicit credential -- otherwise you get exactly the cross-account bleed this whole mechanism is designed to prevent. This is a large, native-touching, cross-cutting rewrite with ongoing maintenance risk against an OS the platform actively fights.
reddit.recommendation: Recommend (A): ACCEPT that Reddit is single-active-account and design Janus's AccountManager around an "active account per source" model with swap-on-switch. The reviewer is CORRECT for Reddit. Hydra's auth rides one process-global native cookie jar (host-keyed reddit_session in NSHTTPCookieStorage) plus one global modhash singleton, and iOS does not give RN JS reliable per-request Cookie control, so two Reddit sessions cannot be live simultaneously through the existing XHR transport. The Janus architecture's assumption that "multiple accounts can be ACTIVE SIMULTANEOUSLY via per-instance adapters" is FALSE for Reddit as built. Concretely: model each source (Reddit, Lemmy) as having at most one active account; switching Reddit accounts is a serial swap -- clear the jar + modhash, restore the target account's session + modhash (exactly Hydra's doWithTempLogout pattern in contexts/AccountContext.tsx lines 69-79, plus restore/save on lines 42/55). Importantly, CROSS-SOURCE concurrency still works: Reddit and Lemmy use different hosts/transports, so one active Reddit account AND one active Lemmy account simultaneously is fine -- the constraint is only "one active account per source," and within Reddit specifically. So the per-instance-adapter design survives if "instance" means "per source," not "per account." Trade-offs: (A) is simplest, matches Hydra today, zero native code, and is low-risk -- the cost is that Reddit account switches are serial (re-auth/restore latency on switch, and you cannot fan out parallel requests as two different Reddit users). (B) buys true concurrent Reddit accounts but requires a native transport rewrite (per-request Cookie injection with httpShouldHandleCookies=NO, redirect re-injection to dodge RN bug #15918/#26311), a per-account modhash refactor, and reworking the WebView login so the shared-jar cookie does not leak as the implicit credential -- high effort, native maintenance burden, and fighting iOS. Recommendation: ship (A) now; only pursue (B) if product genuinely needs simultaneous multi-Reddit-account live sessions (e.g., parallel cross-account actions), which is a niche need that does not justify the native rewrite for v1.

Verified against the installed package: pure-ESM, single entry (dist/index.mjs, 134KB runtime), zero occurrences of window/document/atob/btoa/localStorage/XMLHttpRequest/node:/fs/process in threadiverse's own dist, and a first-class injectable fetchFunction (index.mjs:3494, :4165) defaulting to globalThis.fetch which RN provides. Auth is a plain headers map (Bearer JWT) with no token-store coupling. PageCursor is number|string with a next_page/prev_page PagableResponse (index.d.ts:2008-2009) that drops straight into TanStack/FlashList getNextPageParam, and the unified Notification inbox + single unread count is the package's biggest value-add. Required shims, all small and scoped: (1) uploadImage is the only real friction — the TS param is the DOM File (index.d.ts:13283) which is undefined under Hermes, but the runtime is permissive: the PieFed path is `new FormData(); append(...)` (index.mjs:4117) and the Lemmy path falls into `new Blob([image],{type:'image/jpeg'})` when `image instanceof File` is false (lemmy-js-client-v0 http.js:1029/1034). Pass an RN FormData descriptor {uri,name,type} TS-cast to File or an RN Blob, replace Voyager's canvas compressor with expo-image-manipulator, and on-device test the pictrs multipart upload before committing. (2) Metro/bundle hygiene for the @tsoa/runtime chain that lemmy-js-client-v1 statically pulls (import at index.mjs:4 -> require('@tsoa/runtime') at http.js:25 -> require('reflect-metadata') at index.js:17): include reflect-metadata (self-installs under Hermes) and add a Metro resolver blockList so the express/@hapi/koa template barrels — referenced only as types, never required at load — do not bloat or noise the bundle; verify with an actual Metro build. (3) transformIgnorePatterns so Metro and Jest treat threadiverse + both lemmy-js-client packages as ESM. NOT needed: base64/URL/DOM polyfills for the client itself. Fallback if @tsoa resolution proves intractable: depend on lemmy-js-client-v0 directly (zero deps) and hand-roll PieFed, sacrificing the auto-detection, unified conversion, consolidated inbox, and Zod validation — only if the Metro spike fails, which is unlikely.
synthesis.redditConcurrencyFinding: The reviewer is correct: Reddit is single-active-account, not multi-active. Confirmed in Hydra source. Auth rides one process-global native cookie jar plus one global modhash singleton: UserAuth.modhash is a static class field (api/Authentication.ts:1-2), the api() chokepoint sets only X-Modhash/User-Agent/Content-Type and never a Cookie header (api/RedditApi.ts:25-41), safeFetch is an XHR wrapper that blindly forwards headers and never sets Cookie or withCredentials (utils/safeFetch.ts:49-56), and the reddit_session cookie is attached implicitly by the iOS native layer (NSURLSession/shared NSHTTPCookieStorage, httpShouldHandleCookies=YES). RedditCookies is the only jar writer/reader and is hardcoded to the single host key https://www.reddit.com (utils/RedditCookies.ts:10-11,22,41,49,65). A grep found zero explicit Cookie headers anywhere in api/ utils/ contexts/. Per-request Cookie control from JS is unreliable on iOS — RN does not expose httpShouldHandleCookies per request and drops cookies/auth headers across redirects (RN bug #15918/#26311), which Reddit's redirect-heavy login hits. So two live Reddit sessions cannot coexist through the existing transport. CRUCIAL nuance that rescues the architecture: cross-source concurrency is fine — Reddit and Lemmy use different hosts/transports, so one active Reddit account AND one active Lemmy account simultaneously works. The constraint is exactly one active account PER SOURCE (and that bites only Reddit). The Janus per-instance-adapter design survives if "instance" means per-source, not per-account. Switching Reddit accounts is a serial swap (clear jar+modhash, restore target's session+modhash) — exactly Hydra's doWithTempLogout pattern (contexts/AccountContext.tsx:42,51,55,69-73). True concurrent multi-Reddit-account would require a native transport rewrite (httpShouldHandleCookies=NO + per-request Cookie injection + redirect re-injection + per-account modhash + ephemeral WebView login store), which is high-effort, native-maintenance-heavy, and fights iOS; not justified for v1.
contractChanges: AccountManager: DROP the 'multiple accounts can be ACTIVE SIMULTANEOUSLY via per-instance adapters' premise. Model exactly one active account PER SOURCE. An 'adapter instance' is bound to a source, not to an account. Cross-source concurrency (1 active Reddit + 1 active Lemmy) is supported; intra-source (2 Reddit) is not.

AccountManager: Reddit account switch is a serial swap operation, not a parallel fan-out. Define switchActiveAccount(source, accountId) as: persist current (session cookie + modhash) -> clear native jar + modhash -> restore target's session + modhash (mirror Hydra's doWithTempLogout/save/restore, AccountContext.tsx:42/51/55/69-73). Expose switch latency / re-auth as an explicit async state, not instantaneous.

SourceAdapter / AccountManager: per-account credentials are owned by the AccountManager, NOT the live transport. For Reddit store reddit_session + per-account modhash in SecureStore; on switch, write into the single host-keyed native jar (CookieManager, host https://www.reddit.com) and set the (formerly global) modhash. The modhash must become per-account state threaded through the swap, not a process-global singleton.

Transport contract: rate-limit + backoff live in the transport layer and the PageRequest contract from PHASE 1 (not Phase 4). Every adapter request flows through a shared transport that owns retry/backoff/429-handling and surfaces rate-limit metadata. For Lemmy this wraps threadiverse's injected fetchFunction; for Reddit it wraps the XHR/safeFetch transport.

SourceAdapter capability flags: capabilities must NOT advertise awards/polls (Hydra stubs these). Capabilities are a per-source declared set the UI gates on; only advertise features the adapter genuinely implements. Add explicit imageUpload capability since the Lemmy/PieFed upload paths differ and RN upload is the highest-risk call.

Domain model — comment LoadMoreRef: redesign as a discriminated union, do NOT use one shape. Variants: {kind:'reddit', childIds:string[]} | {kind:'lemmy-subtree', parentId:number} | {kind:'count-only', missingCount:number}. The single conflated ref (Reddit childIds vs Lemmy parent_id-subtree vs child_count-missing) is invalid.

Domain model — JanusId: separate canonicalId (keyed on local instance, for routing/display) from dedupKey (the federation ap_id, for cross-instance dedup). Dedup/merge MUST key on ap_id, not the local-instance id, so the same federated post/comment seen via different home instances collapses correctly.

Pagination contract: adopt threadiverse's opaque PageCursor = number | string directly as the cross-source cursor type (verified index.d.ts:2008-2009). PageRequest carries an opaque cursor; PageResponse carries nextCursor (from next_page). Do NOT model page numbers — Lemmy/PieFed differ and the opaque cursor unifies them and Reddit's after-token.

Notification contract: adopt threadiverse's unified Notification model (single kind discriminator: subscribed|private_message|mod_action|reply|mention) as the Janus inbox abstraction for the Lemmy source rather than hand-rolling; AccountManager exposes one inbox stream + one unread count per active account.

uploadImage contract: the SourceAdapter upload method must accept an RN file descriptor {uri,name,type} (or RN Blob), NOT a DOM File. The adapter internally TS-casts to satisfy threadiverse's File-typed param. Mark this path as requiring an on-device pictrs smoke test before the adapter is considered done.

openDecisionsForUser.decision: Reddit account concurrency model for v1: accept single-active-account-per-source (serial swap) or invest in a native transport rewrite for true concurrent Reddit sessions?
options: A) Single-active-account per source with serial swap-on-switch (zero native code, matches Hydra, low risk)
B) Native transport rewrite: httpShouldHandleCookies=NO + per-request Cookie injection + redirect re-injection (#15918/#26311) + per-account modhash + isolated WebView login store
openDecisionsForUser.recommendation: A. Ship single-active-account-per-source now. Cross-source concurrency (1 Reddit + 1 Lemmy live) still works, so the per-source-instance adapter design holds. Only pursue B if the product later genuinely needs simultaneous live multi-Reddit-account sessions (parallel cross-account actions) — a niche need that does not justify fighting iOS for v1.

options: Run a dedicated on-device uploadImage spike (RN FormData {uri,name,type} on PieFed path + RN Blob on Lemmy instanceof-File-false branch) before LemmyAdapter work
Defer and discover during Phase 1 adapter implementation
openDecisionsForUser.recommendation: Spike before. It is the single highest-risk call (DOM File type vs Hermes, RN FormData/Blob multipart semantics are historically finicky). A half-day on-device spike retires the only real threadiverse risk and de-risks the whole adapter.

openDecisionsForUser.decision: Image compression library to replace Voyager's canvas-based compressor (helpers/imageCompress.ts is browser-only and not usable in RN)?
options: no client-side compression (upload original, let server handle)
openDecisionsForUser.recommendation: expo-image-manipulator — first-party Expo, RN-native, produces a file URI that feeds straight into the {uri,name,type} FormData descriptor, and avoids any DOM/canvas dependency.

openDecisionsForUser.decision: Where does the WebView Reddit login deposit the captured session given the single-active-account model?
options: Keep Hydra's shared-jar approach: login writes reddit_session into the shared native store, app reads it as the active account (simplest, matches Hydra)
Capture-and-evict: read the cookie post-login, persist per-account to SecureStore, and manage the live jar explicitly via swap
openDecisionsForUser.recommendation: Capture-and-evict into SecureStore, but still drive the live jar through the AccountManager swap. Even in single-active mode this gives clean per-account persistence and makes a future move to option B (true concurrency) far cheaper, without the cross-account cookie bleed the shared jar risks when multiple accounts are stored.
